subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Gulliver's Travels and Satirical Worlds
description: One-minute skill: Gulliver's Travels and Satirical Worlds.

hook.text: Jonathan Swift wrote a children's adventure that was actually a savage attack on all of human civilization.

buildup.text: Gulliver's Travels sent its hero to tiny people, giants, flying islands, and a land ruled by horses.

discovery.text: Published in 1726, it became an instant bestseller even though most readers missed the deeper satire.

twist.text: Swift portrayed humans as filthy, irrational creatures inferior to the noble horse-people called Houyhnhnms.

climax.text: The novel invented modern political satire and proved fiction could critique power without being censored.

punchline.text: A travel story about tiny people attacked an empire.

quiz.question: What was the true purpose of Gulliver's Travels?
options: To entertain children with fantasy adventures
To satirize human civilization and political power
